description: Track tool versions in Dockerfile ENV lines via '# datasource/depName' comments.
Carries no datasourceTemplate on purpose: a '<field>Template' wins over the
capture group of the same name — createDependency() takes the template branch
first and the capture only as its else — so the 'docker' template that used to
sit here made the (?<datasource>) capture dead code. Every annotated ENV resolved
against the Docker datasource instead of the one its comment named:
'# golang-version/go' was looked up as the image 'go' and the pin never moved,
silently. FROM lines are left to the built-in dockerfile manager.
See https://docs.renovatebot.com/configuration-options/#matchstringsstrategy
Track tool versions in Makefiles via '# renovate: datasource=X depName=Y' comments.
See https://docs.renovatebot.com/configuration-options/#matchstringsstrategy
Renovate config for projects ivuorinen manages
Automerge non-breaking version bumps via branch strategy.
'digest' is deliberately excluded: digest updates bypass minimumReleaseAge
entirely (Renovate pushes them outside filterInternalChecks), so automerging
them would silently accept a force-moved third-party action tag — the exact
attack helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests exists to prevent. Third-party digest
updates therefore raise a reviewable PR; only ivuorinen/actions digests
automerge, via the trusted-source rule at the end of this array.
Exempt git submodules from the global minimumReleaseAge hold. The git-refs
datasource returns no releaseTimestamp, and minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour defaults
to 'timestamp-required', so an unexempted submodule update is marked pending
forever and no branch is ever created. Every other datasource keeps the
fail-closed 3-day hold.
.nvmrc (nvm manager) and pre-commit hook updates change local tooling and CI,
never a package's public API, so they get their own 'tooling' scope — 'actions'
is reserved for GitHub Actions. The default 'deps' scope made semantic-release
in the consuming repo cut a patch for every Node bump
(ivuorinen/base-configs#577 and ivuorinen/base-configs-commitlint#196 were
retitled by hand), and the global major rule's 'chore(deps)!: ' cut a major.
semantic-release-config has a release rule for 'deps' only, so
'chore(tooling): ' releases nothing — as long as it carries no '!'. The prefix
is literal for the same reason as the actions major rule below: a packageRule
can only override the major rule's prefix, not unset it. A repo whose .nvmrc
does ship to users (e.g. a Docker image built from it) overrides this locally.
devDependencies (npm) and require-dev (Composer) never reach a package's
consumers, so no update to one — major included — is a breaking change. The
global major rule's 'chore(deps)!: ' made semantic-release in the consuming repo
cut a major for a test-runner bump. semantic-release-config has a release rule
for 'deps' only, so 'chore(dev-deps): ' releases nothing. The prefix is literal
because a packageRule can only override the major rule's prefix, not unset it;
semanticCommitScope is set to match so the two never disagree. Must stay after
the major rule: later matching rules win.
Re-enable digest updates for ALL GitHub Actions.
helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests pins every action to a SHA, but the global
digest.enabled:false would otherwise freeze those pinned SHAs forever when
a floating tag (e.g. @v1) moves to a new commit. This keeps digests disabled
for Docker and everything else, while letting all actions stay current.
Enabling a digest update is not the same as automerging it: third-party
action digests raise a reviewable PR, and only ivuorinen/actions digests
inherit automerge from the trusted-source rule at the end of this array.
Never mark a GitHub Actions major bump as a breaking change. The global major
rule sets 'chore(deps)!: ', and the '!' makes semantic-release in the consuming
repo cut a major release — but an actions/checkout v4 → v5 bump changes CI only,
never the package's public API. This restates the prefix literally rather than
resetting it, because a packageRule can only override a value, not unset one;
the literal must stay in sync with semanticCommitType + the 'actions'
semanticCommitScope set above. Must stay after the major rule: later matching
rules win.
Group the annotated tool pins — Makefile variables and workflow '*_VERSION' env
vars — into one PR. The workflow paths cover the customManagers:githubActionsVersions
preset in 'extends': those deps come from the custom.regex manager, not the
github-actions one, so the actions rules above never match them. Narrower than the
preset extracts, on purpose: it also reads Gitea/Forgejo workflows and
workflow-templates, which no repo here uses. Those still update, just ungrouped.
Every ecosystem group below, and the '@ivuorinen packages' group, appends
' (dev)' to its name for devDependencies and require-dev. The dev-deps rule
gives dev updates 'chore(dev-deps): ' (no release) while runtime updates keep
'chore(deps)', and a grouped branch takes its commitMessagePrefix from the
first upgrade sorted by depName (Renovate's generateBranchConfig). A group
holding both would title a runtime bump 'chore(dev-deps)' whenever a dev
package sorted first, and semantic-release would never ship it. groupName is
compiled as a template per upgrade, so the suffix splits the group into its
own branch and PR. test/check-commit-messages.mjs asserts every group that can
mix dependency types carries the suffix.
Fast-track first-party packages. This rule and the three below MUST stay last
in packageRules: the ecosystem groups above match on unanchored regexes
(/eslint/, /stylelint/, /semantic-release/) which also match
@ivuorinen/eslint-config, @ivuorinen/stylelint-config, @ivuorinen/stylelint-a11y
and @ivuorinen/semantic-release-config. Renovate applies packageRules in array
order and later matches win, so placed earlier this groupName was silently
overwritten for a third of the scope. Grouping, priority and the release-age
waiver apply to every update type; automerge is granted separately below.
Automerge first-party packages, minor and patch only. Majors are excluded on
purpose: this rule waives the 3-day minimumReleaseAge and the non-office-hours
schedule, so an automerged major would reach every consuming repo within one
Renovate run with no cooldown and no human in the loop — the same reasoning
this repo's own .github/renovate.json applies to renovatebot/** ('a major bump
can rename or drop the hook id. Majors get a review'). First-party majors still
get an immediate, top-priority PR from the rule above; they just need a click.
Fast-track first-party actions. Grouping, priority and the release-age waiver
apply to every update type; automerge is granted separately below.
Automerge first-party actions. 'digest' is included here and nowhere else: this
is the trusted source whose digest updates are allowed to automerge, while
third-party action digests deliberately raise a reviewable PR. Majors are
excluded for the same reason as first-party packages above.
